about: Pass 12 held-items pass, part A (2026-10-11). Owner decision 2026-10-11: 'just use the data if we can please. only thing that should hold us back is licensing.' Input: the held_for_owner arrays of pass4-visual-llm, pass6-charxiv, pass6-tau2telecom, pass6-tbhard, pass7-lone-A..E and pass8-new-sources (81 triage entries; the tbhard item is split into 3). Every imported value was re-read at its pinned source on 2026-10-11 (HTML/PDF text, committed CSV/TSV/JSON/parquet, or printed digits in committed chart/table images, which the owner allowed on 2026-10-09); nothing was copied from the earlier held notes. 'triage' has one entry per input item; 'results'/'benchmarks'/'models'/'ledger' are in the usual seed shape (apply-pass2.mjs + npm run import); 'edits' lists changes to existing data the import cannot make (one ledger merge, one source_id fill, one bin-consistency note); 'extracts' holds the CC BY-SA rows (CharXiv paper test split, Canary/Parakeet report) for a data/extracts file; held_for_owner lists only cells kept for licence, identity or not-printed reasons. hivemind-32b-preview and qwen-agentworld-35b-a3b do not occur in these files. Validated in a scratch copy: apply-pass2 + npm run import (+9 models, +836 results, +18 benchmarks) and node scripts/check.ts --validate-only pass; npm test matches the unmodified copy (only the pages-link test fails, because the copy omits pages/).

benchmarks.name: Polyrating rating (bias-aware re-fit of Chatbot Arena votes, mid-2024)
benchmarks.description: Polyrating main rating (Elo scale) from Table 7 of arXiv 2409.00696v3: the authors refit the public Chatbot Arena pairwise human votes (114 models, up to mid-2024) with a multidimensional Bradley-Terry model that separates response quality from task/prompt-type modifiers (English, Chinese, hardness, code). Same votes as lmarena-text, different rating model and snapshot; not merged with lmarena-text.

benchmarks.name: CharXiv reasoning questions (test split)
benchmarks.description: CharXiv reasoning-question accuracy on the held-out TEST split (1,323 charts, answers kept private, scored by the CharXiv authors), as printed in Appendix C Table 4 of arXiv:2406.18521v1. Different questions from charxiv-rq (validation split); not merged with it.

benchmarks.name: CharXiv descriptive questions (test split)
benchmarks.description: CharXiv descriptive-question accuracy on the held-out TEST split (1,323 charts, answers kept private, scored by the CharXiv authors), as printed in Appendix C Table 4 of arXiv:2406.18521v1. Different questions from charxiv-dq (validation split); not merged with it.

benchmarks.name: ChineseWord (LongCat-Image 8,105-character set, PPOCRv5) overall
benchmarks.description: Chinese character rendering accuracy on the 8,105-prompt ChineseWord set built by the LongCat-Image authors (one prompt per character of the General Standard Chinese Characters Table, standardized template, following Qwen-Image's protocol), scored with PPOCRv5 OCR; Overall accuracy over levels L1-L3, divided by 100. Not Qwen-Image's own ChineseWord numbers.

benchmarks.name: QCRI Arabic-English ASR leaderboard, 22-set average WER
benchmarks.description: Average WER (fraction) over the 22 Arabic, English and code-switched test sets of QCRI's bilingual ASR leaderboard (arzen, Casablanca, Common Voice ar (+AURA split), DACS, ESCWA code-switch, EveryAyah, FLEURS ar/code-switch/en, L2-ARCTIC, LibriSpeech test-clean/other, MASC clean/noisy, MGB-2/3/5, Mixat, QASR code-switch, RDI, SADA), scored by QCRI with one bilingual normalizer (diacritics removed, Alef variants unified, punctuation removed, Latin lower-cased). As printed in the 'Average WER' column.

benchmarks.name: AHELM VoxCeleb2 same-speaker detection (exact match)
benchmarks.description: Audio-LLM task from AHELM (Stanford CRFM, HELM framework): given two VoxCeleb2 audio clips, answer whether the speakers are the same; exact-match accuracy, temperature 0. Not an ASR test. Source: AHELM, arXiv 2508.21376v2 (CC BY 4.0).

benchmarks.name: AHELM VocalSound human-sound recognition (prefix exact match)
benchmarks.description: AHELM scenario: recognise the human vocal sound in a VocalSound clip (laughter, sigh, cough, throat clearing, sneeze, sniff); pseudo/prefix exact match, temperature 0. Source: AHELM, arXiv 2508.21376v2 (CC BY 4.0).

benchmarks.name: AHELM LibriSpeech transcription by audio LLMs (WER)
benchmarks.description: AHELM scenario: an audio-language model is prompted to transcribe LibriSpeech audio; word error rate (fraction, lower is better), temperature 0, max 200 output tokens. For audio LLMs (category llm); dedicated speech recognisers are scored on the stt benchmarks instead. Source: AHELM, arXiv 2508.21376v2 (CC BY 4.0).

benchmarks.name: AHELM AIR-Bench Foundation music subsets (exact match)
benchmarks.description: AHELM knowledge scenario: AIR-Bench (Foundation) single-choice questions, music subsets only (music genre recognition, instrument classification, music QA); exact match, temperature 0. Source: AHELM, arXiv 2508.21376v2 (CC BY 4.0).

benchmarks.name: AHELM CoRe-Bench conversational audio reasoning (pseudo-exact match)
benchmarks.description: CoRe-Bench, introduced in the AHELM paper: 2,290 questions over 2,082 synthetic multi-turn audio conversations whose answers must be inferred from the dialogue; pseudo-exact match, temperature 0. Source: AHELM, arXiv 2508.21376v2 (CC BY 4.0).

benchmarks.name: AHELM MELD audio emotion classification (pseudo-exact match)
benchmarks.description: AHELM emotion scenario: classify one of seven emotions (anger, disgust, sadness, joy, neutral, surprise, fear) from MELD (Friends) audio clips only; pseudo-exact match, temperature 0. Source: AHELM, arXiv 2508.21376v2 (CC BY 4.0).

benchmarks.name: AHELM MUStARD audio sarcasm detection (exact match)
benchmarks.description: AHELM emotion scenario: detect sarcasm from the audio of MUStARD sitcom utterances (with context); binary exact match, temperature 0. Source: AHELM, arXiv 2508.21376v2 (CC BY 4.0).

benchmarks.name: AHELM FLEURS 7-language transcription by audio LLMs (WER)
benchmarks.description: AHELM multilinguality scenario: transcribe FLEURS audio in Finnish, Mandarin Chinese, Thai, Hebrew, Bengali, English and Zulu; mean WER (fraction; can exceed 1 when models produce long hallucinated output), temperature 0, max 200 output tokens. Source: AHELM, arXiv 2508.21376v2 (CC BY 4.0).

benchmarks.name: AHELM Multilingual LibriSpeech 7-language transcription by audio LLMs (WER)
benchmarks.description: AHELM multilinguality scenario: transcribe Multilingual LibriSpeech audio in Italian, French, Polish, Dutch, Portuguese, Spanish and German; mean WER (fraction), temperature 0. Source: AHELM, arXiv 2508.21376v2 (CC BY 4.0).

benchmarks.name: AHELM Speech Robust Bench (LibriSpeech-clean with noise) transcription WER
benchmarks.description: AHELM robustness scenario: transcribe LibriSpeech-clean audio from Speech Robust Bench with Gaussian or environmental noise at levels 1-3 (four subsets); mean WER (fraction), temperature 0. Source: AHELM, arXiv 2508.21376v2 (CC BY 4.0).

benchmarks.name: HaluEval QA hallucination detection (accuracy)
benchmarks.description: HaluEval QA split as run in the Hallucinations Leaderboard (lm-eval task 'halueval_qa'): given a knowledge passage, question and answer, decide whether the answer contains a hallucination (yes/no); accuracy over 10,000 samples.

benchmarks.name: MedQA (USMLE, 4 options)
benchmarks.description: MedQA USMLE-style medical exam questions, English 4-option test set (1,273 questions), zero-shot accuracy by likelihood ranking (lm-eval task 'medqa_4options').

benchmarks.name: MedMCQA
benchmarks.description: MedMCQA Indian medical entrance exam questions (4 options), validation split (4,183 questions), zero-shot accuracy by likelihood ranking (lm-eval task 'medmcqa').
